EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The 60-day US-Iran "Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding" has expired without a comprehensive agreement, leading Iran to declare a shift to a "fully offensive" policy and set a deadline of "several weeks" for the US, threatening regional escalation. Concurrently, an Emirati tanker was detained in the Strait of Hormuz, while US President Trump issued explicit threats against Oman over its engagement in talks concerning the strategic waterway.

IRAN
Iran has formally declared a shift from a defensive posture to a "fully offensive" policy, setting a deadline of "several weeks" for the full implementation of its Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the United States. A senior Iranian official conveyed that all Iranian entities are prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and across the region if diplomatic efforts fail. IRGC Political Deputy General Javani stated that the Strait of Hormuz will only reopen once the US ends its "war against Iran" in line with the Islamabad MoU. US intelligence (Wall Street Journal) indicates Tehran is preparing for a wider confrontation, accelerating missile and drone production, tightening IRGC control, and coordinating potential escalation with allied militias in Yemen and Iraq, including discussions of pre-emptive strikes and attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure.

On the domestic front, President Pezeshkian emphasized patience, solidarity, and hope as key to Iran's resilience. The judiciary has announced stricter enforcement regarding hijab and online activities. The economic situation remains challenging, with reports of a severe shortage and rising prices of medicines, while insurance companies are reportedly delaying payments to pharmacies. Trump claimed Iran is experiencing 300% inflation, although this figure is unverified by other sources. Trump also asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz via a naval blockade, claiming to be extracting millions of barrels of oil weekly. The US Central Command reported diverting 64 commercial vessels and disabling three since the naval blockade's resumption. An Emirati tanker was stopped near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz for alleged regulation violations. Iranian Minister of Roads and Urban Development stated that approximately 100 commercial aircraft were damaged, with eight completely destroyed, during what was referred to as "the war against Iran." A large fire erupted in Gorgan, destroying over 20 shops, with electrical short circuits cited as a probable cause.

ISRAEL
The Israeli military conducted strikes in the northern Gaza Strip following a Hamas bomb explosion and gunfire on the Israeli side of the "Yellow Line," which the IDF labeled a ceasefire violation. Syrian sources reported an Israeli aerial attack on Abu al-Duhur military airport in Idlib, northern Syria. In southern Lebanon, Israeli airstrikes were reported in Mansouri and Deir Siryan, and Israeli forces carried out controlled detonations in Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Bani Hayyan. No Israeli casualties were reported in the Gaza incident.

Domestically, the Likud party primaries concluded with a 53.5% voter turnout; final results are anticipated tomorrow morning, August 19. Initial tallies suggest significant changes, with ministers Avi Dichter, Idit Silman, and May Golan likely losing their Knesset seats, and others like Ze'ev Elkin, Gila Gamliel, and Nir Barkat facing challenging re-election bids. Prime Minister Netanyahu did not extend voting hours, a departure from past practice. Netanyahu and Jared Kushner discussed the Gaza situation, with the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) announcing an agreement with the "Peace Council" to form two working groups. One group will focus on the complete disarmament and demilitarization of Gaza, including the removal of all weapons and tunnels, which is a precondition for any reconstruction. The second group will address sanitation and public health. Israel explicitly reserves the right to self-defense and freedom of action. Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that the IDF would present a plan within two weeks to transfer civilian enforcement responsibilities in the West Bank to the Israeli Police. Separately, Naftali Bennett claimed Israel is halting defense exports to Qatar, which he characterized as an "enemy state," despite previously approving hundreds of millions of dollars in such exports.

Tragic civilian incidents occurred in Beit Shemesh, where 7-year-old Hillel Mordechai Dadon was stabbed to death and his 4-year-old cousin critically injured by a mentally unstable neighbor. Another 4-year-old child was killed in a separate traffic accident in the same city. In Hadera, a one-year-old infant sustained severe head injuries after falling from playground equipment. A medical scandal emerged involving a fertility patient who discovered her newborn's biological father was not the intended sperm donor.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, a Hamas bomb detonated on the Israeli side of the "Yellow Line" in the north, accompanied by gunfire, which the IDF declared a violation of the ceasefire. The IDF responded with retaliatory strikes in the area. Jared Kushner met with Hamas officials, stating that "all the right things were said," but emphasized the difficulty of trusting a terror organization and reiterated that Gaza's reconstruction would not proceed until it is demilitarized. Hamas, through its representative in Tehran, Khalid Qaddoumi, maintains that resistance and weapons will persist as long as the occupation exists, rejecting disarmament as a precondition for any deal. Hamas welcomed Trump's call for an Israeli ceasefire and urged him to pressure Israel to implement Phase 2 of his Gaza plan.

In the West Bank, IDF forces from the Menashe Brigade conducted an operation in the Qabatiya village, scanning approximately 100 structures and arresting two individuals suspected of promoting terror plots against Israelis and security forces. Near Nablus (Shechem), reserve soldiers arrested a wanted individual in possession of rifles, incitement materials, and a large sum of money (150,000 NIS), thwarting an imminent terror attack. Israeli forces have maintained a nine-day siege on Qusra, declaring it a closed military zone and restricting access to essential supplies. Settler activity continued, with reports of main roads being blocked and Palestinian vehicles attacked near Efrat, south of Bethlehem.

LEBANON
Israeli airstrikes were reported in Mansouri and Deir Siryan in southern Lebanon. Additionally, Israeli forces carried out controlled detonations in Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Bani Hayyan, also in southern Lebanon. No specific Hezbollah operations were reported in the given timeframe.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan, two drones, identified as Hadid-110, targeted the private office of Prime Minister Masrour Barzani and the residence of the Director of the Protection Agency. The Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism Directorate reported that these drones were launched from inside Iran, although no casualties occurred. Iran's Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei strongly condemned the attack, calling it a "false-flag plot" designed to sow discord, and vehemently denied any Iranian involvement. The Iraqi Prime Minister has initiated an investigation into the incident. Separately, Iraqi Air Force F-16s conducted two successful airstrikes, though targets were not specified.

Syrian reports indicated an Israeli aerial attack on the Abu al-Duhur military airport in the Idlib countryside. In southern Iraq, government forces were reportedly deploying heavily in Maysan province for unknown reasons. A massive fire erupted at a fuel storage tank in Sulaymaniyah, northern Iraq, injuring 18 people. An American surveillance balloon was observed and subsequently re-deployed by US forces over Erbil province. The Iraqi Prime Minister stated that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has significantly reduced Iraq's oil exports. Iraqi plans to export oil via a pipeline through Syria are estimated to take four years and cost $15 billion. Militant activity included Houthi claims of attacking a Saudi military ship and four escorts near Mocha, Yemen. In Baghdad, protests erupted in Dhi Qar following the abduction of an intelligence official from the Hashd al-Shaabi paramilitary forces.

GULF STATES
Tensions escalated in the Gulf region as an Emirati tanker was stopped near Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz for alleged regulation violations. Trump explicitly threatened to bomb Oman if it interfered with negotiations regarding the Strait of Hormuz. Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed to have attacked a Saudi military amphibious ship and four accompanying military boats in the Red Sea, vowing to maintain a "siege for siege" approach. Saudi Arabia temporarily halted its oil exports from the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait due to increased insecurity. The Wall Street Journal reported that Gulf states, including Kuwait, are increasingly concerned about Iran's plans for "offensive operations in enemy territory." Kuwait also reported that three feeders from its Rumaithiya B substation went offline. The Middle East aviation industry is facing a crisis due to the "war against Iran," with Gulf airlines like those in the UAE and Qatar potentially losing their geographical advantage as an air bridge between East and West.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran MOU Expiration and Escalation Threat**: The 60-day US-Iran "Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding" expired without a comprehensive agreement. Iran announced a shift to a "fully offensive" policy and set a "several weeks" deadline for US implementation of the MOU, threatening regional escalation.
2.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions**: An Emirati tanker was stopped near Iran's Qeshm Island for alleged regulation violations, while US President Trump threatened to bomb Oman if it interfered with negotiations regarding the Strait of Hormuz.
3.  **Gaza Disarmament Standoff**: Israel and the "Peace Council" agreed that Gaza's reconstruction is contingent on the complete disarmament and demilitarization of Hamas (all weapons and tunnels removed). Hamas, however, rejected disarmament as a precondition for any deal.
4.  **Erbil Drone Attack**: Two Hadid-110 drones targeted the office of Kurdistan Region PM Masrour Barzani and the Protection Agency Director's residence in Erbil. The Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism Directorate claimed the drones were launched from Iran, a claim Iran strongly denied, labeling it a "false-flag plot."
5.  **Likud Primary Shake-Up**: Preliminary results from the Israeli Likud primaries (53.5% turnout) indicate significant changes in party leadership, with several incumbent ministers (Avi Dichter, Idit Silman, May Golan) likely losing their Knesset seats.
6.  **Beit Shemesh Stabbing**: A 7-year-old child, Hillel Mordechai Dadon, was stabbed to death, and his 4-year-old cousin critically injured, in Beit Shemesh by a mentally unstable neighbor, who was subsequently arrested.
7.  **Trump's Approval Low and Nuclear War Claims**: US President Trump's approval rating dropped to a historic low of 33% amid public concern over the "war of aggression against Iran." Former US Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene claimed discussions about nuclear strikes on Iran occurred in Trump administration meetings.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation in the Middle East is HIGH. Iran's declared shift to a "fully offensive" policy, coupled with a "several weeks" deadline for the US, signals a willingness for military action. Flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where an Emirati tanker was detained and Trump issued direct threats against Oman. The expiration of the US-Iran MOU without a resolution further exacerbates these tensions. US intelligence reports indicate Iran is preparing for wider confrontation, including potential pre-emptive strikes and attacks on Gulf infrastructure. The drone attack in Erbil, regardless of perpetrator, adds to regional instability and mutual accusations. In Gaza, Hamas's rejection of disarmament, juxtaposed with Israeli demands and continued operations, ensures ongoing conflict. Trump reiterated that preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons remains the US's "number one goal," establishing a critical red line. Freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz is another key red line for the US.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
US President Trump's approval rating has plummeted to a historic low of 33%, with a majority of Americans expressing concern over the "war of aggression against Iran." Trump publicly threatened to bomb Oman if it interfered in Strait of Hormuz negotiations and claimed the US controls the strait through a blockade. Jared Kushner is attempting to advance a Gaza roadmap through discussions with both Hamas and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, facing challenges over Hamas's disarmament. The Pentagon has reportedly concluded that no military plan can guarantee safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Among Gulf states, Saudi Arabia halted oil exports from Bab al-Mandab due to insecurity, and an Emirati tanker was detained by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait and other Gulf states are reportedly concerned about Iran's plans for offensive operations. In Europe, Latvia is seeking €7 billion from the EU to offset military and economic costs related to the conflict with Russia. Russia canceled a military music festival in Moscow and sentenced an opposition figure to 11.5 years for "discrediting the army," while Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov stated North Korean forces are fighting alongside Russia in Kursk. China will host King Abdullah II of Jordan and is preparing for a meeting between President Xi Jinping and President Trump on September 24. Turkish President Erdoğan engaged with Trump on Iran and Gaza, offering to mediate, and separately discussed the Strait of Hormuz with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding US-Iran communications: President Trump claimed "secret backchannel communications with the IRGC," which the IRGC vehemently denied as "delusions." Conflicting reports also emerged on the status of the Strait of Hormuz; Trump stated it is "open" and oil prices are falling, while US Energy Secretary Chris Wright reported a nearly 20% decrease in traffic and the Iraqi Prime Minister claimed the strait's closure has severely reduced Iraqi oil exports. Additionally, Trump's assertion of "no hurry" for a deal with Iran contrasts with a senior Iranian official's statement of a "several weeks" deadline for US MOU implementation.

Unverified claims include the Kurdistan Counter-Terrorism Directorate's assertion that drones targeting Masrour Barzani's office were "launched from Iran," a claim strongly refuted by Iran. Former US Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene's claim about discussions of nuclear strikes on Iran in Trump administration meetings remains unconfirmed. Propaganda indicators are evident in Trump's inflammatory rhetoric towards Iran and Speaker Qalibaf's unsubstantiated claims of Iranian victory. Reporting gaps include the precise terms of the expired US-Iran "Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding" and the composition and authority of the "Peace Council" engaged in Gaza negotiations.
